candidates.existing: Competitor search (query 18) found no filing software or service; only law-firm reminders. The state offers no free filing tool that I saw.
candidates.name: Charitable trust annual return and audited-accounts filing pack
candidates.trigger: Charitable Trusts Act s.29A (inserted 2013): yearly return to the Registrar with trustee and office-bearer list and audited accounts; the Registrar cancels incorporation after a Gazette notice and 21-day notices; names may be published.
candidates.unchecked: Number of registered trusts; whether the Registrar has an online filing portal; the audit cost barrier (unaudited small trusts may not be able to pay for a tool); willingness to pay.

candidates.buyer: Minibus, carrier and taxi PSV permit holders
candidates.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
candidates.existing: No software seen. The one-off change creates no recurring filing.
candidates.name: PSV permit transfer ban and permit-holder compliance tracker
candidates.trigger: LTA regulations gazetted 13 March 2026 ban permit transfers by sale; transfers only for family, migration, medical grounds or death; pending transfers cancelled.
candidates.unchecked: Number of permit holders; renewal duties; whether any recurring reporting exists.

candidates.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
candidates.evidence: https://www.fijitimes.com.fj/?p=458366; https://www.fbcnews.com.fj/?p=705810; https://wikiprocedure.com/index.php/Fiji_-_Renewal_of_Driving_School_License (unofficial, fees may be outdated)
candidates.existing: No software seen; no competitor search run for this idea (search budget used).
candidates.name: Driving school and instructor permit renewal and compliance pack
candidates.trigger: LTA instructor permit (annual renewal, about $400 per instructor reported by the former association president); March 2025 crackdown cancelled 14 driving school permits; diploma requirement for new applicants.
candidates.unchecked: Number of schools and instructors; whether permits moved to three years; current LTA fees; competitor search.

candidates.existing: None seen. A recruiter in April 2026 proposed stricter accreditation.
candidates.name: Overseas recruitment agency authorisation and placement register
candidates.trigger: Employment Relations Act 2007 and Employment Agencies Regulations 2008: Permanent Secretary authorisation, advertising rules, ongoing monitoring; UN CMW asked Fiji about licensing and monitoring.
candidates.unchecked: Number of authorised agencies (reported as very small); PALM-scheme reporting duties; reporting forms.

candidates.name: Scrap metal dealer licence and purchase register
candidates.trigger: Scrap Metal Trade Decree/Act 2011: dealer licence from the Ministry of Trade; offences for buying public infrastructure metal; Nov 2024 suspension of non-ferrous scrap trade (except gold) and a taskforce.
candidates.unchecked: Whether the dealer must keep a seller register (the Act's record-keeping sections were not read); current status of the suspension; number of licensed dealers.

candidates.buyer: Private cemetery and crematorium operators, funeral services
candidates.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
candidates.name: Burial ground and crematorium licensing under the Burial and Cremation Amendment Bill 2025
candidates.trigger: Bill No. 30 of 2025 would modernise licensing and management and raise fines for unlicensed burial from $200 to $5,000; passage and commencement not confirmed.
candidates.unchecked: Whether the bill passed; number of private operators (the Corrections Service runs many cemeteries); any recurring reporting.

candidates.buyer: Waste haulers, septic and tanker operators, and the firms that hire them
candidates.existing: Consultancies (Environment Consultants Fiji) sell permit help; no software seen.
candidates.name: Waste Disposal Permit and waste transporter compliance
candidates.trigger: Environment Management Act 2005 and Waste Disposal and Recycling Regulation 2007 (Waste Disposal Permit); WAF Liquid Trade Waste Policy covers tankers; Feb and Apr 2026 enforcement cases against a company using an unlicensed transporter.
candidates.unchecked: Whether a transporter register exists; permit reporting frequency; number of haulers.

candidates.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
candidates.existing: None seen. No dealer-level periodic report found, so this is an inspection risk, not a filing duty.
candidates.name: Pesticide retailer registered-product check
candidates.trigger: Pesticides Act 1971: only registered pesticides may be sold; the Ministry confiscates repacked or unregistered products from retailers.
candidates.unchecked: Any retailer licence or sales return; number of retailers.

candidates.name: Registered slaughterhouse and butcher meat-source records
candidates.trigger: Meat Industry Act (Cap 237): meat may only be sold from registered slaughterhouses; inspector must attend rural slaughter (2015 regulation amendment); Food Safety Act health licence for shops.
candidates.unchecked: Whether butchers must keep a purchase register; the Act's replacement status.

candidates.existing: BAF handles it on a paper form. Tiny user base.
candidates.name: Beekeeper apiary movement application
candidates.trigger: BAF Apiculture Movement Application Form (2021); Varroa emergency order of 2020 banning hive movement without approval (has likely lapsed).
candidates.unchecked: Number of beekeepers; whether the Varroa order was renewed.

candidates.buyer: Money changers and Restricted Foreign Exchange Dealers
candidates.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
candidates.name: Licensed money changer and restricted FX dealer RBF reporting
candidates.trigger: RBF licence under the Exchange Control Act; revised operational guidelines (May 2025): capital limits, overnight cash limit of 75% of paid-up capital, reporting to the RBF and FIU.
candidates.unchecked: Number of licensees (probably under 20); reporting format and whether the RBF has its own portal.

candidates.existing: Competitor search (query 20): businessNOW FIJI government portal handles health licence application and renewal with e-certificates, 14-day target. This weakens the idea; whether the health licence service is fully live is unconfirmed.

candidates.unchecked: Portal health licence live status; whether permit renewal reminders and document packs add value.

coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K14. Minimum wage F$5/hr (reported, from 1 Apr 2025); FNPF registration duty for employees aged 15+. No source specific to households. Employment Relations Act 2007 under revision (unconfirmed).

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: Scrap Metal Trade Decree/Act 2011 requires a dealer licence (Ministry of Trade; Forms & Fees Regs 2011). Nov 2024 suspension of non-ferrous scrap trade (except gold) and a taskforce (Recycling Today); still in force or not is unconfirmed. Small, enforcement-driven; candidate C05.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No Fiji second-hand dealers or pawnbroker statute surfaced in the search. Unverified. Not reached beyond one query.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: No Fiji licensing rule for gold or jewellery buyers found. Only the Nov 2024 non-ferrous scrap suspension, which exempts gold. Unverified.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No Fiji-specific dismantler licensing found (only NZ/AU results). The LTA has expanded inspection agencies by outsourcing, which is a separate matter.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K13. Meat Industry Act (Cap 237) governs slaughter, and the Board's 2015 report says the Act is outdated. No livestock-trader register found.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Meat Industry Act: meat must come from registered slaughterhouses; rural slaughterhouses need an inspector present (2015 regulation amendment). Food Safety Act health licence applies to butcher shops. No butcher-specific software gap found; candidate C09 (weak).

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: BAF Apiculture Movement Application Form (2021) and an AFB surveillance form exist. The 2020 Varroa emergency order has likely lapsed (unconfirmed). Tiny paper-form workflow with a handful of users; candidate C10 (weak).

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: No Fiji vet-medicine register or reporting rule found. A very small market. Unverified.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: The Mineral Resources Dept drills state boreholes. A Groundwater Resources Development and Management Policy and a National Water Resources Management and Sanitation Policy are pending. No driller licence or abstraction licence found.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Environment Management Act 2005 plus the 2007 Waste Disposal and Recycling Regulation (Waste Disposal Permit). WAF Liquid Trade Waste Policy covers tankers. 2026 enforcement against a company using an unlicensed transporter. No hauler register or software found; candidate C07 (weak).

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: The Health and Safety at Work Act 1996 (National OHS Service) ties OHS compliance inspection to business licence renewal. No boiler, pressure vessel or lift registration found. Unverified.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: WAF runs urban and most rural supply; no private small-system regulator register found in the search budget.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: The Pesticides Act 1971 requires every pesticide sold to be registered with the Registrar (Koronivia). The Ministry confiscates unregistered or repacked pesticides from retailers (2023-24). A product register, not a dealer-reporting duty; candidate C08 (weak).

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Overseas recruitment agencies need Permanent Secretary authorisation under the Employment Relations Act 2007 and the Employment Agencies Regulations 2008. Very few authorised agencies (April 2026 report). UN CMW has asked about licensing and monitoring. Candidate C04 (weak: tiny buyer base).

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: The Burial and Cremation Act is a 1911 law. Burial and Cremation (Amendment) Bill No. 30 of 2025 would modernise licensing of cemeteries and crematoria and raise fines for unlicensed burial from $200 to $5,000; passage not confirmed. The Corrections Service runs many cemeteries. Candidate C06 (weak).

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Charitable Trusts Act s.29A requires an annual return with audited accounts; non-filers are cancelled after a Gazette notice (705 organisations listed in 2021). Candidate C01. The Fiji Muslim League runs halal certification and launched a Digital Halal Ecosystem in Oct 2024 with the IsDB, so the halal side is covered; candidate C10b is not needed.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Taxi base/stand reform: K04 (existing operators must secure bases by 30 Sept 2027; permits only to individuals; $30k household income test). New PSV permit transfer ban gazetted 13 March 2026. Bus operators: 53 operators, 1,218 buses, QAMS audits and a bi-annual fleet audit, so the market is too small. Candidates C02, C03.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Municipal market licences (draft 2020 regs: $1,000 a year, $1,500 for fish) and fee waivers are council-run; Cabinet approved stall charges for the new Nakasi Market (Jan 2025). Money changers and Restricted FX Dealers: RBF licensing under the Exchange Control Act, revised operational guidelines (May 2025), reporting to the RBF and FIU. Very few licensees; candidate C11 (weak).

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Driving schools: the LTA cancelled 14 permits in March 2025, stricter instructor rules, about $400 a year renewal per instructor (candidate C03). Food premises health licence renews yearly by January (Food Safety Act 2003, penalty up to $10,000), but the businessNOW FIJI portal handles application and renewal (candidate C12). ECE centres: Ministry of Education approval, 764 to over 1,000 centres (candidate C13). Tattoo: no licence yet, Public Health Act review pending. Hunting outfitters not applicable.
